_fields.as_of: the date the figure was last read from, or confirmed against, that source
_fields.note: what a reader of the number needs to know: config, fallbacks, restatements
_fields.history: the pull log that used to live in code comments above each array, oldest first; append to it on every re-check
_fields.board: id of the third-party board in board-checks.json that this chart is checked against
_fields.drift: aeci chart, second panel: `released` is each model's public release date (from models.json; the panel's x position), `fits` is the cards in release order (the fit each one used), `values` every AECI value printed in a card; `own` marks the value in the model's own card, lo/hi the 95% (global) interval where printed, n the number of benchmarks the model was scored on
_fields.estimated / derivation: aeci chart: `estimated` marks a value this site computed, not a published one; `derivation` (provenance, not written to the page) holds the original value, its fit, the overlap pairs and the mapping
_fields.figure_read / anchor: chart data on the aeci chart: a value measured off a published figure (approximate, drawn hollow), and the scale's fixed anchor
_fields.reported_by: chart data, not provenance: set to "anthropic" on a row of a board-sourced chart whose figure comes from Anthropic's own report because the board has not listed it yet. The chart draws such a point hollow; delete the field when the board lists the row
_fields.everything else on a row: chart data, copied into the page as written

Where a later card restates a model under the newer setup, that figure is plotted. With-tools figures, per-effort figures and both outside boards are recorded, not plotted.
caveats: Every plotted point is first-party. Outside boards run different question subsets and score far lower or slightly differently: see `other_sources`.
No-tools and with-tools runs are different evaluations and are never joined.
Thinking settings moved from fixed budgets (Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5, Haiku 4.5) to adaptive/auto thinking at max effort; the token cap went from 1M to a 980k task budget. Anthropic grades with Opus 4.6.
The answer key is disputed in places (FutureHouse, 2025), so the practical ceiling is below 100%.
history: 2026-11-09: chart added. Three sources were weighed for the plotted series. (a) Anthropic's system cards: a no-tools and a with-tools figure for 17 Claude models from Sonnet 4.5 (Sep 2025) to Fable 5.2, read from the local index system-cards/metrics.json (metric humanitys-last-exam; each card's own entry plus the comparison figures it restates), and the Fable 5.2 card's Table 8.1.A and sec. 8.11.1 re-read in the card text. (b) Artificial Analysis: HLE values for seven Claude models only (Fable 5, Opus 5, Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5.2), all max-effort entries, on AA's 2,158 text-only questions; the payload read today carries no hle value for any Claude model before Fable 5. AA files the benchmark under 'Legacy'. (c) Scale AI / CAIS leaderboard: 18 Claude rows back to Claude 3.5 Sonnet (Oct 2024) but none for Opus 4.8, Fable 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Opus 5.5 or Fable 5.2, with thinking and non-thinking rows mixed and effort stated on only some. Its page header now describes the HLE-Rolling fork (update of September 17, 2026); which rows were scored on which revision was not established. The cards give the longest history under one family of setups, so the chart plots the cards' no-tools figures; (b) and (c) are recorded under `other_sources` and described in the note, not plotted.

Rule for restated figures: where a later card re-reports an earlier model beside its own under the newer setup and the number differs from that model's own card, the restated figure is plotted and the own-card figure is in the row note (Sonnet 4.6 34.6 vs 33.2, Sonnet 5 43.1 vs 43.2, Opus 5 56.6 vs 56.3). Fable 5, Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5, Opus 4.6 and Haiku 4.5 have no no-tools number in their own cards and are plotted from the first card that states one.

With-tools figures are in each row's note, not on the chart: the tool setup changed across cards (context compaction up to 3M tokens through Mythos Preview, a 1M-token cap from Opus 4.7, a restricted fetch tool and a growing blocklist, cheating re-grades), so that series is less like-for-like than the no-tools one, and for the newest model the two are a point apart (73.2 vs 74.2).

aeci.source: Fable 5.2 / Mythos 5.2 system card, sec. 2.3.5: Table 2.3.5.3.A and Figure 2.3.5.3.B, the November 6, 2026 fit
aeci.plot_rule: `points` is ONE fit: every row comes from the same card, except rows flagged estimated (see caveats). Rows with lo/hi are the card's table (lo/hi = global 95% CI, localLo/localHi = local CI). Rows flagged figure_read were measured off the card's figure and have no interval; the row flagged anchor is 130 by definition. Replace the whole list when a newer card publishes a new fit.

Mythos models are the restricted twins of the Fable releases; Fable is not scored separately.

history: 2026-11-09: chart added from the Fable 5.2 / Mythos 5.2 system card, sec. 2.3.5 (pp. 35-39), read in the card text and PDF. Table 2.3.5.3.A, the November 6 fit (371 benchmarks, 10,803 observations, 1,026 models), gives six released Claude models with global and local 95% intervals, plus an unreleased 'Internal Model' at 178.78 [173.75, 185.18] (local [177.08, 180.59], scored on 15 benchmarks), which is in the note and not on the chart because it has no public date. Mythos 5.2 is scored on 37 benchmarks 'using an earlier snapshot'.

One fit only. The card: 'Because each refit reestimates the whole scale, AECI values from this fit are not comparable to the AECI values in earlier system cards ... Comparisons between models should be made within a single fit.' So nothing from an earlier card is appended; those values are under `earlier_fits`. That is why Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Opus 4.8 and Opus 4.7 are absent: each was scored only in a different fit. WHEN THE NEXT CARD SHIPS: replace `points` whole with that card's table; never append to it.

Figure 2.3.5.3.B plots eight earlier frontier models by name with no printed values: Claude 3 Opus, 3.5 Sonnet (the 130 anchor), 3.5 Sonnet (new), 3.7 Sonnet, Opus 4, Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5 and Opus 4.6. Seven are added as figure reads (`figure_read`, drawn hollow, no interval), measured from a 400-dpi render; the method reproduces the three tabled models that the figure labels and the anchor to within 0.1. Fable, Haiku and Sonnet 5.x models are not in the figure.

Dates: the card plots models on their internal availability date ('the same date convention used in METR's independent assessment'). This chart uses public release dates from models.json like every other chart on the page, so slopes read off it are not the card's.

Trend, as the card states it: fitted slope change about 1.88x in October 2025 (95% CI 1.62x-2.28x across 100 refits), 'nominally below the 2x threshold set in our RSP, but the estimate varies considerably depending on which benchmarks and model snapshots are included in the fit'; figure legend: frontier trend 15.3/yr to 28.7/yr at the fitted breakpoint, against 16.2/yr with a fitted +8.8 jump at Mythos Preview. Mythos 5.2 is 'about 11 points above the historical trend line and 2.3 points above Claude Opus 5.5'. The one-time-jump fit has the lower error in 0 of 100 refits (16 excluding the internal model, 63 excluding it and Mythos 5.2). The trend lines are not redrawn here.

Estimates added 2026-11-09 at the owner's request: Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 were scored only in their own cards' fits, each of which also states Opus 5.5 (169.12 and 174.56). Shifting by Opus 5.5's move to the November 6 fit (174.78) gives Sonnet 5.5 167.93 + 5.66 = 173.6 and Haiku 5.5 167.11 + 0.22 = 167.3, each shown with a +/-1.0 range taken from the spread of offsets in the September 18 -> November 6 overlaps (Opus 5 165.18 -> 169.40, Mythos 5.1 168.12 -> 172.62, Opus 5.5 169.36 -> 174.78). Overlap values verified against the card index (metric anthropic-eci). Deliberately not estimated: Opus 4.8 (155.5) and Opus 4.7 (154.1), from the Opus 4.8 card's n=11 fit. That card does state Mythos Preview (158.3, vs 165.71 here), but the owner's instruction was not to reach back to that fit: 11 benchmarks, five refits ago, one overlap. Each estimated row carries `derivation`. When `points` is replaced for a new fit, drop these rows or re-derive them.

Refit-drift panel added 2026-11-09. Every AECI value Anthropic has printed, in text or a table, in any system card: re-read today in the PDFs of the Mythos Preview, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, Fable 5 / Mythos 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.2 / Mythos 5.2 cards (pdftotext of the files at the URLs in scripts/build-system-cards.py). 25 values, 10 models, 8 cards, under `drift`. The Mythos Preview and Opus 4.7 cards print no absolute value (slope ratios 1.86x-4.3x; Opus 4.7 'approximately +1.0' above trend, Mythos Preview +5.8), so those two models have no own-card point. The Sonnet 5 card: 'we did not compile AECI for Sonnet 5'. Every card from Mythos Preview on also has a figure plotting earlier models, none with printed value labels; apart from the November 6 figure read for the main panel, figures were not measured, so the matrix has gaps where a card shows a model only as a dot. The Opus 5.5 card rounds two earlier values when quoting them (Mythos 5.1 '162.0', Opus 5 '160.7'); the originals are recorded. The estimates in `points` use overlap pairs that are cells of this matrix (Opus 5.5 at 169.12, 174.56 and 174.78).

history: Capability Profile — radar/spider chart across ten evaluations, one polygon per family's newest model (Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5). Form borrowed from Thinking Machines' Inkling launch chart, restyled to this page's palette. Rebuilt 2026-09-28: Artificial Analysis had reworked its suite (no GPQA Diamond or Terminal-Bench 2.1 runs for the newest models, Agentic Index retired, Omniscience published only as a -100..100 index) and Vals had no LiveCodeBench run for Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5, so every axis here is one all four models have.
Re-pulled whole 2026-11-09, when Fable 5.2 shipped, so no shape mixes snapshots.

Nine from AA, read 2026-11-09 from the model records embedded in artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/gdpval-aa (initialModels), each model's max-effort entry ("Claude Fable 5.2 (Max, Default Fallback)", "Claude Opus 5.5 (Max, Default Fallback)", "Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Max, Default Fallback)", "Claude Haiku 5.5 (Max)"): Terminal-Bench 4.0 (terminalBench40), AutomationBench-AA (automationBenchPartialScore: objectives completed without guardrail violations), GDP.pdf (gdpPdfAllPass), Harvey LAB (harveyLabBreakdown .criteriaPass, the mean criterion-pass rate; AA's headline harveyLab field is the far lower all-pass rate), CritPt, HealthBench Professional (healthbenchProfessionalBreakdown.score, the raw score; the same field's lengthAdjustedScore is 67.7 / 59.9 / 63.0 / 58.4), HLE, AA-LCR (v1.1) and SciCode. On that read Harvey LAB had been re-scored about a point lower than on Sep 28 (Opus 5.5 91.2 -> 90.0, Sonnet 5.5 93.1 -> 92.1) and Sonnet 5.5's AutomationBench had moved 71.3 -> 71.8; every other Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 value matched Sep 28.

One from Anthropic's system cards. SWE-bench Pro: Fable 5.2 93.0 (Fable 5.2 / Mythos 5.2 card, Table 8.1.A, which repeats Opus 5.5 89.9), Sonnet 5.5 81.3 (Sonnet 5.5 card), Haiku 5.5 64.8 (Haiku 5.5 card).

HealthBench Professional was a second system-card axis until 2026-11-09 (Opus 5.5 65.6, Fable 5.1 62.1, Sonnet 5.5 69.2: Anthropic's runs, graded by Opus 4.8). The Fable 5.2 card (sec. 8.16) reports AA's runs instead (graded by GPT-5.4) and says they are not comparable with the earlier cards, so the axis moved to AA for all four models. The card's raw scores match AA's records: Fable 5.2 71.1, Opus 5.5 71.4, Sonnet 5.5 70.8, Haiku 5.5 64.8.

Haiku 4.5 stood in for Haiku until this read: on 2026-10-10 AA showed only an Intelligence Index for Haiku 5.5. Fable 5.1 and Haiku 4.5 are no longer plotted. Mythos 5.2 is not plotted: its published capability figures are Anthropic's no-safeguards runs (Terminal-Bench 4.0 70.5 among them), with no AA entry.

A null score is a documented gap, never a zero: the series is drawn as an open polyline with no marker at that vertex. No current model needs one (Haiku 4.5 did, on HealthBench), but the drawing code keeps the case.

history: Remote Labor Index — share of 240 real freelance projects completed to a standard a paying client would accept. Figures from the Scale AI / CAIS leaderboard and the accompanying CAIS write-up, pulled 2026-07-29; the two agree on every Claude entry (Fable 5: write-up 15.8%, board 15.83%). Opus 5 shipped after the July results.

Re-checked 2026-10-10 (labs.scale.com/leaderboard/rli, embedded entries JSON): two new Claude rows, Opus 5.5 21.25% (rank 1, flagged NEW, createdAt 2026-10-07) and Fable 5.1 17.92% (rank 3, createdAt 2026-09-17), both plotted below; GPT 6 Astra sits between them at 20.83%. No row for Opus 5, Sonnet 5 or 5.5, Haiku 4.5 or 5.5, or any Mythos. The board gives no harness or budget for the two new runs.

Re-checked 2026-11-09: no Fable 5.2 row; every Claude row above unchanged (Opus 5.5 still rank 1 on the board). The Fable 5.2 / Mythos 5.2 system card (sec. 8.14.7, Table 8.1.A) reports 41.3% (99/240) from a Scale-run evaluation at Scale's defaults (high effort, 200k-token context, 32k tokens per response).

2026-11-09, later the same day: Fable 5.2 is now plotted from that system-card figure, as a hollow point joined to the Fable line by a dashed segment, flagged `reported_by: "anthropic"`. Reason: it is the same Scale-run evaluation the board publishes, and the card's other columns (Fable 5.1 17.9, Opus 5.5 21.3, GPT-6 Astra 20.8) match the board (17.92, 21.25, 20.83) to rounding, so this is a Scale result Anthropic published before Scale's board listed it. Every other row is still read from the board. When the board lists Fable 5.2: replace the score with the board's figure, delete `reported_by`, update `source`, and the point turns solid. Caution kept in the note: 17.9 to 41.3 in ten weeks is far larger than any other step on the chart, the runs do not share a harness, and the board gives no harness details for the Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 runs.
